Date: 2027-01-08
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Lila Moreno (Northbridge), Evan Zhou (SRE), Sofia Alvarez (CTO), Marco Diaz (Security)
summary: Discovery focused on Northbridge Health's need for reserved GPU capacity with strict isolation and HIPAA-like controls. Important topics: sustained vs burst traffic patterns, VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM encryption, audit logs, prewarm/hot-pool strategy, fallback policies to hosted models, and expected SLA/uptime requirements. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated but needs clarity on failover cost and multi-region residency for EU patients.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump into your workload and constraints.
[00:12] Lila (Northbridge): Hi, I'm Lila, head of ML at Northbridge Health. We build triage and summarization models for patient notes, lots of PHI so HIPAA compliance is mandatory.
[00:22] Jordan: Got it. Priya, want to intro yourself?
[00:25] Priya (Redwood): Sure, Priya Patel, I'm a solutions engineer working on inference ops — latency, batching, KV cache stuff. Excited to dig in.
[00:33] Evan (SRE): Evan here. Running infra and observability. Main constraint is we cannot have PHI leave our VPC unless encrypted and logged, and we want tenant isolation across teams.
[00:43] Sofia (CTO): Hi, Sofia — timeline is Q2 pilot, production late Q3, budget conversations already started. We want a predictably priced dedicated option.
[00:52] Jordan: Thanks. Quick agenda: sizing + burst, isolation/VPC, compliance (KMS, audit logs), fallback plan. Sound good?
[00:58] Lila: Yep.
[01:02] Jordan: Can you walk us through traffic? Avg RPS, tails, peak behavior?
[01:08] Lila: Our baseline for the triage model is ~20 qps during business hours, but we have a long-tail: sudden spikes after clinical release notes, or appointment batch runs where we see spikes to ~350 qps for 5-15 minutes a few times a week. Also nightly batch summarization — heavy but asynchronous.
[01:25] Priya: When you say spikes, is it concurrent short requests, or multi-token streaming long sessions? That affects KV cah — sorry, K-V cash — the cache hit patterns.
[01:34] Lila: Mostly short requests, 100-500 tokens each. Some streaming for live note dictation but that's smaller percent.
[01:40] Evan: We'll need prewarm for the short, bursty spikes so latency doesn't tank, and we want guaranteed isolation for our production tenant.
[01:48] Sofia: Also, residency: EU patients must stay in EU region. Could be multi-region deployment.
[01:54] Priya: Ok. For Dedicated we do reserved GPU pools with options for warm pools / hot pools for prewarmed models. We can size reserved nodes for baseline and then allow burst to a hot pool or to hosted fallback. Have you evaluated on-prem vs VPC?
[02:09] Marco (Security): Security is critical. We require customer-controlled KMS and HSM-backed key wrap. Audit logs that show per-request token-level metadata for at least 90 days. SOC2 is table stakes, and we may need ISO 27001. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS?
[02:25] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated (hosted but dedicated pool) can integrate via VPC peering and bring-your-own-key patterns; we'll confirm exact key wrap flows.
[02:36] Lila: If we do Dedicated hosted with VPC, what's the blast radius? We don't want noisy tenants to affect our latency.
[02:44] Priya: We offer tenant fencing and strict pod/node-level isolation in Dedicated. For highest isolation we recommend isolated instance pools — effectively single-tenant nodes. That increases cost but reduces noisy neighbor risk.
[02:55] Evan: How do prewarm and hot-pool billing work? If we keep a hot pool on standby that's expensive. Would Redwood charge by GPU-hour or by active token usage?
[03:05] Jordan: Dedicated pricing is a hybrid: reserved node pricing (monthly) plus usage-based burst fees. Hot pools are billed as reserved capacity if you want them always on. We can model options in the spreadsheet.
[03:16] Lila: And fallback — if our Dedicated pool is saturated, do requests fail or route to hosted variants? We cannot send PHI to hosted models.
[03:24] Priya: Right — by policy you can configure automatic fallback to either a hosted non-PII model or queue/slow-path. For PHI workloads we recommend no automatic hosted fallback; instead use a queued fallback with guaranteed SLAs or route to an on-prem backup.
[03:39] Sofia: What's the cold-start latency if we spin up a node? For scheduled nightly batches we can cold-start, but for sudden spikes we need <250ms 95th for short prompts.
[03:49] Priya: Cold start to an idle GPU depends on model size. For a 13B-ish model with quantization, warmup can be 3-6s; hot pool prewarmed can give sub-200ms token latency. We can show benchmark numbers in the workshop.
[04:05] Evan: We also need catastrophic failover plan: if a whole region is down, can we failover to another region with residency constraints? For EU patients we can't.
[04:13] Marco: Right — data residency means failover strategy must be region-aware; EU data must stay in EU. We may accept cross-region fallback only for non-EU data.
[04:22] Jordan: That matches patterns we've seen: multi-region deployment with sticky routing and per-region reserved pools. For EU residency we recommend a dedicated EU pool and a separate contract.
[04:34] Lila: For encryption, will Redwood accept our HSM and perform E2E key wrap? We don't want keys on Redwood-managed HSMs.
[04:42] Priya: We support customer-managed key wrap via KMS integrations for Private and for Dedicated with VPC peering; on-prem package allows full customer control. We'll circulate a technical note on the integration patterns.
[04:55] Evan: Observability — we need token-level cost breakdown and request tracing tied to our request ids.
[05:02] Jordan: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, traces, and error analysis. For Dedicated we can export logs to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/EFK) and share retention policies.
[05:13] Marco: What about audit logs and immutability for compliance?
[05:16] Priya: We can write WORM-style logs to customer-owned buckets via VPC endpoints, and integrate with your SIEM. Audit events include model version, timestamp, route, and token counts. We should confirm the exact schema.
[05:26] Lila: One more, prompts and prompt engineering: some of our prompts include PHI. Are prompts stored?
[05:31] Jordan: For Dedicated we can disable retention of prompts or store them in customer-controlled storage. We'll include retention options in the security doc.
[05:39] Sofia: Ok, budget — we're looking for ballpark numbers: reserved node that covers 20qps baseline and the ability to burst to 350qps for short windows. Also need EU region and one US region.
[05:51] Priya: We'll run a cost model: size baseline as N instances (we'll propose node types), add warm-pool sizing for expected burst concurrency, and show cost delta for single-tenant nodes.
[06:01] Jordan: We'll also include an option for a small on-prem test cluster — that helps with drift and compliance for pilot.
[06:07] Evan: For the pilot metrics: we'll measure 95th latency under 250ms for short prompts, token cost per 1k tokens, and failover recovery time under 2 minutes.
[06:16] Lila: Agreed.
[06:18] Jordan: Great — next steps summary — I'll send pricing + burst modeling, Priya will schedule a 2-hour benchmark workshop where we run a representative traffic trace and prewarm experiments. You'll share traffic traces and SOC/KMS requirements. Anything else?
[06:32] Marco: Please include a note on responsibility matrix for key custody and audit log ownership.
[06:37] Jordan: Noted.
[06:39] Sofia: One more question — competitors: we've looked at RunAI and a few managed offerings but we prefer a partner that will handle most of inference plumbing.
[06:48] Jordan: Understood. We'll put a competitive differentiation note in the follow-up.
[06:52] Lila: Thanks everyone.
[06:54] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs this week.
[06:58] [call ends]
